project_overview: This project appears to be a Vue.js application focused on managing exam-related processes, including form submissions, result display, and user interactions. The codebase consists primarily of Vue components, suggesting a component-based architecture. The dependency graph reveals a relatively tight coupling between components, particularly around the 'ApplicationServices' core logic and several user-facing form components. There's a notable concentration of components related to exam and transaction management, indicating a domain-specific focus.

layers.description: Handles user interaction and displays data.
Contains the core application logic for exam and transaction management.

macro_trends.title: Potential State Management Issues
macro_trends.description: Several components, particularly those dealing with exam submissions and transactions (ExamFormSubmission, Transactions, SelectedApplicationService), are heavily reliant on 'Router push' navigation, potentially leading to tight coupling and challenges in managing state across the application. A deep dive into how state is being handled in these components is warranted.

macro_trends.title: UI Consistency Concerns - Accessibility
macro_trends.description: The high number of UI-related issues (Accessibility) across multiple components suggests a potential lack of standardized UI components or style guidelines, leading to inconsistencies and accessibility problems. Component 'ApplicationServices.vue' and 'ExamFormSubmission.vue' especially require attention.

key_workflows.name: Exam Submission Workflow
key_workflows.description: This workflow starts with the user submitting an exam form via 'ExamFormSubmission.vue', transitions through various intermediate steps (potentially using other components), and culminates in displaying the results via 'ResultPage.vue' and 'SelectedApplicationService.vue'. The tight connections here highlight potential bottlenecks and areas for optimization.
